title: The AI-Era PM CV Rulebook
subtitle: ATS & Workday-compliant formatting rules + the STAR framework for writing bullet points, compiled from current ATS/Workday guidance.

star_framework.name: STAR
star_framework.description: Every strong resume bullet should compress a STAR story into one line. On a CV, Situation/Task are often implied by the role and role context, so the visible bullet usually leads with Action and always ends with a quantified Result.

components.label: Situation
components.guidance: The context or problem you faced. Often implied by your job title/section on a resume — spell it out only if it adds critical context (e.g., 'During a 40% YoY drop in activation...').

components.label: Task
components.guidance: What you were responsible for or what needed to happen. Usually folded into the Action clause on a resume bullet.

components.label: Action
components.guidance: The specific thing YOU did — always lead with a strong, specific action verb. Avoid vague verbs like 'worked on' or 'helped with'.

components.label: Result
components.guidance: The quantified outcome: %, $, time saved, users impacted, retention/NPS/revenue change. If you truly cannot quantify, describe the qualitative business outcome (e.g., 'unblocking Series B due diligence').

star_framework.formula: [Action Verb] + [What you built/led/changed] + [Method or tool, if relevant] + [Quantified Result / business impact]
star_framework.good_example: Led discovery and launch of an LLM-based ticket-triage feature, cutting average support resolution time by 32% (4.1 → 2.8 hrs) across a 40-person support org.
star_framework.weak_example: Responsible for working on AI features for the support team and helping improve response times.

formatting_rules.why: Workday and most ATS parsers read left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Multi-column layouts, text boxes, and tables get scrambled or dropped entirely.

formatting_rules.rule: Use standard section headings: 'Professional Experience' (or 'Work Experience'), 'Education', 'Skills', 'Summary', 'Certifications'.
formatting_rules.why: ATS field-mapping looks for these exact/near-exact headings. Creative headings like 'My Journey' or 'What I Bring' may not map to the right resume field.

formatting_rules.rule: Avoid photos, icons, logos, charts, and skill-rating graphics (e.g., star/bar ratings).
formatting_rules.why: Images are invisible to ATS text parsers and can cause parsing errors or push the ATS to reject the file outright.

formatting_rules.rule: Keep contact info (name, phone, email, LinkedIn) in the main document body, not in a header/footer.
formatting_rules.why: Many ATS engines (including some Workday configurations) don't reliably parse headers/footers, so your contact details can silently vanish.

formatting_rules.rule: Use a common, ATS-safe font (Arial, Calibri, Garamond, Georgia, Helvetica) at 10–12pt body / 14–16pt name.
formatting_rules.why: Decorative or embedded custom fonts may not render/parse correctly and can look broken once converted to plain text.

formatting_rules.rule: Save/export as .docx unless the posting explicitly asks for PDF; if PDF, use a text-based (not scanned/image) PDF.
formatting_rules.why: Workday and many ATS platforms parse .docx most reliably. Image-based PDFs can't be parsed at all.

formatting_rules.rule: Name the file 'FirstName_LastName_Resume.docx' (or similar) — no special characters, emojis, or version tags like 'FINAL_v3'.
formatting_rules.why: Clean file names parse better and look more professional to a recruiter opening it after ATS screening.

formatting_rules.rule: Use reverse-chronological order within each section (most recent first).
formatting_rules.why: This is the format ATS parsers and recruiters expect by default; functional/skills-first formats often confuse date-field parsing.

formatting_rules.rule: Use a single, consistent date format throughout (e.g., 'Jan 2023 – Present').
formatting_rules.why: Inconsistent date formats can break ATS date-range parsing used for experience-length filters.

formatting_rules.rule: Use simple round or square bullet characters (•, -). Avoid custom icon bullets or emoji.
formatting_rules.why: Non-standard bullet glyphs can render as garbled characters (e.g., '?' or boxes) once parsed as plain text.

formatting_rules.rule: Don't use tables for laying out experience or skills.
formatting_rules.why: Table cell order is often read out of sequence by ATS parsers, scrambling your work history.

content_rules.rule: Write every bullet in STAR form, leading with a strong action verb and ending with a quantified result.
content_rules.why: Recruiters and hiring managers spend ~6–8 seconds on first pass; quantified impact is what gets a bullet re-read.

content_rules.rule: Never open a bullet with 'Responsible for', 'Worked on', 'Helped with', 'Involved in', 'Duties included', or 'Assisted'.
content_rules.why: These describe a job description, not an accomplishment, and read as passive/low-ownership to both ATS keyword scoring and humans.

content_rules.rule: Quantify at least 70–80% of your bullets: %, $, time, users, NPS/CSAT, headcount, model accuracy, latency, etc.
content_rules.why: Numbers are the fastest proxy for impact a reader (human or AI-assisted recruiter tool) uses to rank candidates.

content_rules.rule: Never use 'I', 'me', 'my', or 'we' — resume bullets are implied first-person.
content_rules.why: Standard resume convention; explicit pronouns read as unpolished and waste character budget.

content_rules.rule: Don't rely on unproven adjectives alone ('detail-oriented', 'hardworking', 'team player', 'results-driven', 'synergy').
content_rules.why: These are unverifiable and heavily overused; if you must use one, immediately back it with a concrete example.

content_rules.rule: Mirror the exact keywords/phrases from the target job description (tool names, methodologies, certifications) wherever true.
content_rules.why: Workday and most ATS platforms rank/filter candidates by keyword match against the JD; synonyms often aren't credited.

content_rules.rule: Spell out an acronym on first use, e.g., 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)'.
content_rules.why: Some ATS keyword search is literal; spelling it out once covers both the acronym and full-term searches.

content_rules.rule: Aim for 1 page (<8 yrs experience) to 2 pages (8+ yrs). Never 3+.
content_rules.why: Recruiter attention and many ATS previews degrade sharply past 2 pages; ruthlessly cut low-impact bullets instead.

content_rules.rule: Keep each bullet to roughly 1–2 lines (~15–30 words).
content_rules.why: Long bullets bury the result; short, fragment-only bullets (<8 words) look thin on evidence.

master_checklist: Standard section headings (Professional Experience, Education, Skills)
Contact info in the document body, not header/footer
Saved as .docx (or text-based PDF if explicitly requested)
Every bullet in Action → Method → Quantified Result form
No 'Responsible for' / 'Worked on' / other weak openers
Keywords mirror the target job description
Acronyms spelled out on first use
